clue.text: Failure of explosive device

definitions.meaning: a flop, as when a show ... at the box office

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: a show that flops is a dud, and a device that detonates is the weapon itself.

clue.text: Epic film about a law-breaker

indicators.note: the epic and film words are placed around the article

parts.note: something epic is big
a film is a thin haze, a mist

explanation.surface: A grand movie is about someone who breaks the law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'film' looks like a movie in the surface, but it is a thin layer of mist.
explanation.definitionFit: A person with two spouses at once commits a crime, so is a particular kind of law-breaker.

clue.text: Welshman perhaps who can't cope with the English?

definitions.text: Welshman perhaps who can't cope with the English?

parts.words: Welshman perhaps who can't cope with the English?
parts.note: pictures a Welsh speaker who knows no English, i.e. someone with only one language

explanation.definitionFit: A person who speaks only one language, such as Welsh alone, is a monolingual speaker.

clue.text: Print showing high portal after refurbishment

indicators.note: something refurbished has been done up and rearranged, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: An engraving depicts a lofty doorway that has recently been restored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after refurbishment' rearranges the ten letters of HIGH PORTAL; 'showing' links fodder and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A print made from a flat stone or metal plate treated with grease and water is a classic kind of printed image.

clue.text: Opening section is not the raciest of openings

indicators.note: the openings of the words are their first letters

explanation.surface: The start of a piece isn't its most exciting part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'openings' takes the first letters of 'is not the raciest of'.
explanation.definitionFit: The introductory passage of a song or show is its opening section.

clue.text: Drinking hard, pleased with our pub's promotion

indicators.note: the pleased word and our take in the letter for hard, as if drinking it

parts.note: happy means pleased
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Drinking heavily, delighted with our pub's special offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drinking hard' reads as heavy boozing, but 'Drinking' is the container signal swallowing the letter for hard; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A happy hour is a period when a bar sells drinks cheaply, a promotional offer.

clue.text: Training beard to develop, take it on the chin

indicators.note: developing means changing form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Grooming a beard to grow it out means accepting something painful on the chin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to develop' rearranges TRAINING BEARD.
explanation.definitionFit: Both idioms mean accepting hardship or misfortune stoically without complaint.

clue.text: A change I introduced in section of zoo

indicators.note: the letter is introduced into the word for change, placed within it

parts.note: to vary is to change

explanation.surface: An alteration made to part of a zoo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'introduced in' puts I inside VARY, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: A large enclosure for birds is a common area within a zoo.

clue.text: Prime crop for farmers colouring up inside

indicators.note: the colouring word goes inside the crop word

parts.note: hay is grass grown and cut for fodder

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: a dye colours things

explanation.surface: Farmers' best crop has colouring rising inside it.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' reverses the colouring word, and 'inside' places that within the farm crop; 'Prime' is an adjective-looking noun meaning peak time.
explanation.definitionFit: One's prime is the period of greatest success or vigour, also called one's peak.

clue.text: Report weapons stolen

parts.note: guns are weapons
hot is slang for stolen goods

explanation.surface: A news item says that firearms have gone missing in a theft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Report' looks like a news story, but it is the bang of a firearm.
explanation.definitionFit: A report is the loud bang a firearm makes when fired, so the sound of a shot fits.

clue.text: Toast church ceremony that's set up to cure us

definitions.text: that's set up to cure us

parts.note: "Your health!" is a toast
a service is a church ceremony

explanation.surface: A drink is raised at a church ceremony arranged to make us well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toast' looks like bread or a verb, but it is the drinking salute.
explanation.definitionFit: A national medical system is an institution organised to treat and heal the public.

clue.text: Invalid, taken short, visits bathroom secretly

indicators.note: one word visiting another goes inside it

parts.note: a privy is an old word for a lavatory

indicators.note: being cut short loses the final letter of the word for ill health

parts.note: an invalid is ill

explanation.surface: A sick person, caught short, slips off to the toilet without anyone noticing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken short' in the surface is the British idiom for urgently needing the toilet, but here it trims the last letter of the word for sick; 'visits' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb is an old-fashioned way of saying privately or in secret, as in being privily informed.

clue.text: Having lots of moves, threatening to take knight with king

indicators.note: the threatening word takes the king in place of the knight, so one letter is swapped for two

parts.note: minatory is a formal word for menacing
N is the chess abbreviation for knight
GR, Georgius Rex, stands for King George

explanation.surface: A chess player menaces to capture a knight using the king, with lots of moves in the game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to take ... with' tells you to swap the N in MINATORY for GR. The chess setting makes 'moves' look like moves in the game, but it means seasonal travel.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals that are migratory make many seasonal journeys, so they have lots of moves.

clue.text: Those without commissions joining army on a vessel

parts.note: OR, other ranks, are soldiers who are not commissioned officers
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: Enlisted soldiers join the army aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' suggests a ship in the military surface, but it is a blood vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: The great artery leaving the heart is the body's largest blood vessel.

clue.text: Talk too loudly? Bookmakers won't, preferring tick-tack

definitions.meaning: to bluster or talk aggressively and opinionatedly
racecourse bookies don't call out prices but signal them by tick-tack, a sign language of hand movements

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to speak loudly and dogmatically, and literally means calling out betting prices, which tick-tack men do silently.

clue.text: Herald finds her garb in disarray

indicators.note: disarray means jumbled, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A messenger discovers that her clothing is in a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disarray' rearranges HER GARB IN; 'finds' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A herald is a forerunner, one who announces something to come.

clue.text: Water — a conserver of it is on offer

parts.note: a dam holds back and conserves water, the 'it' of the clue
goods in a sale are on offer

explanation.surface: Water: a reservoir of it is being sold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' refers back to 'Water'; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a jocular old name for plain drinking water, the only drink of the first man.

clue.text: Goodness! Old soak is making up some borage

parts.note: my! is an exclamation of surprise
a soak is a drunkard, a sot

explanation.surface: Goodness! An old drunk is concocting some herbs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making up' links the pieces to the definition. Borage is a plant family including the forget-me-not.
explanation.definitionFit: The forget-me-not genus belongs to the borage family, so it is an example of that plant group.

clue.text: Flyer insured when up in the air — that's easy to understand

indicators.note: things up in the air are thrown about and unsettled, so these letters are mixed

explanation.surface: An airline passenger is covered by insurance while flying, which makes things simple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when up in the air' rearranges FLYER INSURED; 'that's' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something designed to be simple for ordinary people to operate or grasp is easy to understand.

clue.text: Government department shows British currency's sound

indicators.note: this word signals that the letters are heard rather than seen

parts.note: B for British plus the euro, the European currency

explanation.surface: An official office displays the noise of British money.
explanation.walkthrough: B plus EURO said aloud gives the spelling of the office word.
explanation.definitionFit: In the US especially, a bureau is an administrative office or government agency.

clue.text: Deciduous tree that shields lane

indicators.note: the words shield the answer, covering it within them

explanation.surface: A leafy tree provides shelter to a narrow road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deciduous tree' looks like the definition, but 'shields' hides the answer in 'deciduouS TREE That'.
explanation.definitionFit: A lane is a narrow road, and the answer is any road in a town.

clue.text: Total put into circulation

explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means complete; as a verb it means to issue counterfeit coins or notes into circulation.

clue.text: Amusing or, possibly, unwitting person

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters could form something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who doesn't know any better may be entertaining, or perhaps not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges AMUSING OR.
explanation.definitionFit: An unknowing, ill-informed person lacks wit in the old sense of knowledge.

clue.text: Time for ironing?

parts.note: the time of day after work suits household chores, and ironing makes clothes smooth and level

explanation.definitionFit: The late part of the day is a time word, and as a participle it also means making smooth and level.

clue.text: On strike, players are untouchable

parts.note: workers who are out are on strike
the cast are the actors in a production

explanation.surface: Actors who have walked out in an industrial dispute become pariahs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are' is a link word joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An untouchable is a social pariah, someone rejected and shunned by society.

clue.text: Well-informed article by Indian in trouble

parts.note: up on a subject means well-informed about it
the is the definite article
the Creek are a Native American people

explanation.surface: A knowledgeable piece written by an Indian finds itself in difficulties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indian' means a Native American people here, not someone from India; 'by' places the pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom, short for being stranded without a paddle, means being in a difficult predicament.

clue.text: Place to eat pap

explanation.definitionFit: Forces personnel eat in a dining room of this name, and the word also means an unappetising mash.
